documents.sanskrit: आत्मा वा इदमेक एवाग्र आसीत् नान्यत् किंचन मिषत् । स ईक्षत लोकान्नु सृजा इति ॥
documents.transliteration: ātmā vā idameka evāgra āsīt nānyat kiṁcana miṣat | sa īkṣata lokānnu sṛjā iti ||
documents.text: In the beginning, this was the Self alone — there was nothing else that blinked. He thought, 'Let me now create the worlds.'

documents.sanskrit: असतो मा सद्गमय तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय ॥
documents.transliteration: asato mā sadgamaya tamaso mā jyotirgamaya mṛtyormā amṛtaṁ gamaya ||
documents.text: Lead me from the unreal to the real. Lead me from darkness to light. Lead me from death to immortality.

documents.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि
documents.transliteration: ahaṁ brahmāsmi
documents.text: I am Brahman (Aham Brahmasmi). This is the Mahavakya declaring the unity of the individual self with the universal Brahman.

documents.sanskrit: नेति नेति
documents.transliteration: neti neti
documents.text: Not this, not this (Neti Neti). Brahman transcends all limiting attributes — the classical Upanishadic method of approaching the Absolute through negation.

documents.sanskrit: विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्म रातिर्दातुः परायणम् ।
documents.transliteration: vijñānamānandaṁ brahma rātirdātuḥ parāyaṇam |
documents.text: Brahman is pure knowledge, pure bliss — the goal of the giver of gifts, the refuge of one who knows and stands firm.

documents.sanskrit: एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासने गार्गि सूर्यचन्द्रमसौ विधृतौ तिष्ठतः ।
documents.transliteration: etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryacandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ |
documents.text: O Gargi, by the command of this Imperishable, the sun and the moon are held in their positions.

documents.sanskrit: अयं आत्मा ब्रह्म ।
documents.transliteration: ayaṁ ātmā brahma |
documents.text: This Atman is Brahman (Ayam Atma Brahma). The third of the four great sayings (Mahavakyas) — the individual soul is identical with the universal consciousness.

documents.sanskrit: मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः ।
documents.transliteration: mana eva manuṣyāṇāṁ kāraṇaṁ bandhamokṣayoḥ |
documents.text: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings.

documents.sanskrit: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वं तत्सत्यं स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो
documents.transliteration: sa ya eṣo'ṇimaitadātmyamidaṁ sarvaṁ tatsatyaṁ sa ātmā tattvamasi śvetaketo
documents.text: That which is the finest essence — in it all that exists has its self. That is the Truth. That is the Self. And that, O Shvetaketu, is what you are. (Tat Tvam Asi)

documents.sanskrit: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् ।
documents.transliteration: yo vai bhūmā tatsukhaṁ nālpe sukhamasti bhūmaiva sukhaṁ bhūmā tveva vijijñāsitavyam |
documents.text: That which is infinite (Bhuma) is happiness. There is no happiness in the finite. Only in the Infinite is there happiness.

documents.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत ।
documents.transliteration: sarvaṁ khalvidaṁ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta |
documents.text: All this is Brahman. From Him all things originate, into Him all things dissolve, and in Him they breathe — meditate on that calmly.

documents.sanskrit: सदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयम् ।
documents.transliteration: sadeva somyedamgra āsīdekamevādvitīyam |
documents.text: In the beginning, O dear one, this was Existence (Sat) alone, one only, without a second.

documents.sanskrit: अध्यापयस्व भगव इति होपससाद सनत्कुमारं नारदः ।
documents.transliteration: adhyāpayasva bhagava iti hopasasāda sanatkumāraṁ nāradaḥ |
documents.text: Narada approached Sanatkumara and said: 'Teach me, O Revered One.'

documents.sanskrit: अथ यदिदमस्मिन् ब्रह्मपुरे दहरं पुण्डरीकं वेश्म दहरोऽस्मिन्नन्तराकाशस्तस्मिन्नेतदन्वेष्टव्यं तद्वाव विजिज्ञासितव्यम् ।
documents.transliteration: atha yadidamasmin brahma pure daharaṁ puṇḍarīkaṁ veśma daharo'sminnantarākāśastasminnetadanveṣṭavyaṁ tadvāva vijijñāsitavyam |
documents.text: Now, in this city of Brahman (the body) there is a small lotus-shaped dwelling. Within it is a small inner space. That which is within that should be sought; that should indeed be known.

documents.sanskrit: ईशा वास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥
documents.transliteration: īśā vāsyamidaṁ sarvaṁ yatkiñca jagatyāṁ jagat | tena tyaktena bhuñjīthā mā gṛdhaḥ kasyasviddhanam ||
documents.text:
By the Lord (isa) enveloped must this all be —

Whatever moving thing there is in the moving world.
With this renounced, thou mayest enjoy.

Covet not the wealth of any one at all.

Non-attachment of deeds on the person of a renouncer

documents.sanskrit:
कु॒र्वन्ने॒वेह कर्मा॑णि जिजीवि॒षेच्छ॒त समाः॑ ।

ए॒वं त्वयि॒ नान्यथे॒तो॑ऽस्ति॒ न कर्म॑ लिप्यते॒ नरे॑
documents.text:
Even while doing deeds here,

One may desire to live a hundred years.

Thus on thee — not otherwise than this is it —

The deed ( karman ) adheres not on the man.

The forbidding future for slayers of the Self

documents.sanskrit:
अ॒सु॒र्या॒ नाम॑ ते लो॒का अ॒न्धेन॒ तम॒सावृ॑ताः ।

तास्ते प्रेत्या॒भिग॑च्छन्ति॒ ये के चा॑त्म॒हनो॒ जनाः॑
documents.text:
Devilish ( asurya2' ) are those worlds called,3
With blind darkness (lamas) covered o’er !

Unto them, on deceasing, go

Whatever folk are slayers of the Self.6

The all-surpassing, paradoxical world-being

documents.sanskrit:
अने॑ज॒देकं॒ मन॑सो॒ जवी॑यो॒ नैन॑द्दे॒वा आ॑प्नुव॒न्पूर्व॒मर्श॑त् ।

तद्धाव॑तो॒ऽन्यानत्ये॑ति॒ तिष्ठ॒त्तस्मि॑न्न॒पो मा॑त॒रिश्वा॑ दधाति
documents.text:
Unmoving, the One ( ekam ) is swifter than the mind.

The sense-powers ( deva ) reached not It, speeding on before.
Past others running, This goes standing.

In It Matarisvan places action.6

documents.sanskrit:
तदे॑जति॒ तन्नै॑जति॒ तद्दू॒रे तद्व॑न्ति॒के ।

तद॒न्तर॑स्य॒ सर्व॑स्य॒ तदु॒ सर्व॑स्यास्य बाह्य॒तः
documents.text:
It moves. It moves not.

It is far, and It is near.

It is within all this,

And It is outside of all this.1

documents.sanskrit:
यस्तु सर्वा॑णि भू॒तान्या॒त्मन्ने॒वानु॒पश्य॑ति ।

स॒र्व॒भू॒तेषु॑ चा॒त्मानं॒ ततो॒ न वि जु॑गुप्सते
documents.text:
Now, he who on all beings

Looks as just (eva) in the Self (Atman),

And on the Self as in all beings — 2
He does not shrink away from Him.3

documents.sanskrit:
यस्मि॒न्त्सर्वा॑णि भू॒तान्या॒त्मैवाभू॑द्विजान॒तः ।

तत्र॒ को मोहः॒ कः शोक॑ एक॒त्वम॑नु॒पश्य॑तः
documents.text:
In whom all beings

Have become just (eva) the Self of the discerner —

Then what delusion ( moha ), what sorrow (soka) is there,
Of him who perceives the unity !

Characteristics of the world-ruler

documents.sanskrit:
स पर्य॑गाच्छु॒क्रम॑का॒यम॑व्र॒णम॑स्नावि॒रशु॒द्धमपा॑पविद्धम् ।

क॒विर्म॑नी॒षी प॑रि॒भूः स्व॑यं॒भूर्या॑थातथ्य॒तोऽर्था॒न्व्य॑द धाच्छाश्व॒तीभ्यः॒ समा॑भ्यः
documents.text:
He has environed. The- bright, the bodiless, the scatheless,
The sinewless, the pure (suddha), unpierced by evil (a-papa-
viddha) !

Wise (kavi), intelligent (manisin), encompassing (paribhu), self-
existent (svayambhu),

Appropriately he distributed objects ( artha ) through the eternal
years.

Transcending, while involving, the antithesis of knowing

documents.sanskrit:
अ॒न्धं तमः॒ प्र वि॑शन्ति॒ येऽवि॑द्यामु॒पास॑ते ।

ततो॒ भूय॑ इव॒ ते तमो॒ य उ॑ वि॒द्याया॑ र॒ताः
documents.text:
Into blind darkness enter they
That worship ignorance ;

Into darkness greater than that, as it were, they
That delight in knowledge.4

documents.sanskrit:
अ॒न्यदे॒वाहुर्वि॒द्यया॒न्यदा॑हु॒रवि॑द्याया ।

इति॑ शुश्रुम॒ धीरा॑णां॒ ये न॒स्तद्वि॑चचक्षि॒रे
documents.text:
Other, indeed, they say, than knowledge!

Other, they say, than non-knowledge ! 5
— Thus we have heard from the wise (dhlra)

Who to us have explained It.0

documents.sanskrit:
॥

वि॒द्यां चावि॑द्यां च॒ यस्तद्वेदो॒भय॑ स॒ह ।

अवि॑द्यया मृ॒त्युं ती॒र्त्वा वि॒द्यया॒मृत॑मश्नुते
documents.text:
Knowledge and non-knowledge —

He who this pair conjointly ( saha ) knows,

With non-knowledge passing over death,

With knowledge wins the immortal.1

The inadequacy of any antithesis of being

documents.sanskrit:
॥

अ॒न्धं तमः॒ प्रवि॑शन्ति॒ येऽसं॑भूतिमु॒पास॑ते ।

ततो॒ भूय॑ इव॒ ते तमो॒ य उ॒ संभू॑त्या र॒ताः
documents.text:
Into blind darkness enter they

Who worship non-becoming ( a-sambkuti ) ;

Into darkness greater than that, as it were, they
Who delight in becoming ( sambhuti ).

documents.sanskrit:
अ॒न्यदे॒वाहुः सं॑भ॒वाद॒न्यदा॑हु॒रसं॑भवात् ।

इति॑ शुश्रुम॒ धीरा॑णां॒ ये न॒स्तद्वि॑चचक्षि॒रे
documents.text:
Other, indeed — they say — than origin (sambhava) !

Other — they say — than non-origin ( a-sambhava ) !

— Thus have we heard from the wise

Who to us have explained It.

Becoming and destruction a fundamental duality

documents.sanskrit:
संभू॑तिं च विना॒शं च॒ यस्तद्वेदो॒भय॑ स॒ह ।

वि॒ना॒शेन॑ मृ॒त्युं ती॒र्त्वा संभू॑त्या॒मृत॑मश्नुते
documents.text:
Becoming ( sambhuti ) and destruction (vinasa) —

He who this pair conjointly (saha) knows,

With destruction passing over death,

With becoming wins the immortal.

A dying person’s prayer

documents.sanskrit:
हि॒र॒ण्मये॑न॒ पात्रे॑ण स॒त्यस्यापि॑हितं॒ मुख॑म् ।

तत्त्वं पू॑ष॒न्नपावृ॑णु स॒त्यध॑र्माय दृ॒ष्टये॑
documents.text:
With a golden vessel

The Real’s face is covered o’er.

That do thou, O Pushan, uncover
For one w'hose lawr is the Real to see.4

documents.sanskrit:
पूषन्नेकर्षे यम सूर्य प्राजापत्य व्यूह रश्मीन्समूह तेजो॒

यत्ते॑ रू॒पं कल्या॑णतमं॒ तत्ते॑ पश्यामि

यो॒ऽसाव॒सौ पुरु॑षः॒ सो॒ऽहम॑स्मि
documents.text:
O Nourisher (pusan), the sole Seer ( ekarsi ), O Con-
troller (yama), O Sun (surya), offspring of Prajapati, spread
forth thy rays ! Gather thy brilliance ( tejas ) ! 5 What is thy

documents.sanskrit:
वा॒युरनि॑लम॒मृत॒मथे॒दं भस्मा॑न्त॒ शरी॑रम् ।

ॐ क्रतो॒ स्मर॑ कृ॒त स्म॑र॒ क्रतो॒ स्मर॑ कृ॒त स्म॑र
documents.text:
[My] breath (vayu) to the immortal wind ( anila)\x
This body then ends in ashes ! Om !

O Purpose ( kra/u 2), remember! The deed (krla) remember!
O Purpose, remember ! The deed remember !

General prayer of petition and adoration

documents.sanskrit:
अग्ने॒ नय॑ सु॒पथा॑ रा॒ये अ॒स्मान्विश्वा॑नि देव व॒युना॑नि वि॒द्वान् ।

यु॒यो॒ध्य॒स्मज्जु॑हुरा॒णमेनो॒ भूयि॑ष्ठां ते॒ नम॑ उ॒क्तिं विधेम
documents.text:
O Agni, by a goodly path to prosperity (rat) lead us,

Thou god who knowest all the ways !

Keep far from us crooked-going sin ( etias ) ! 3

Most ample expression of adoration to thee would we render ! 4

documents.sanskrit: ॐ उशन्ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ । तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस
documents.text:
Now verily, with zeal did Vajasravasa give his whole
possession [as a religious gift]. He had a son, Naciketas by
name.

documents.sanskrit: त ह कुमार सन्तं दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धाविवेश सोऽमन्यत
documents.text:
Into him, boy as he was, while the sacrificial gifts were
being led up, faith ( sraddha ) entered. He thought to himself:

documents.sanskrit:
पीतोदका जग्धतृणा दुग्धदोहा निरिन्द्रियाः ।
अनन्दा नाम ते लोकास्तान्स गच्छति ता ददत्
documents.text:
‘ Their water drunk, their grass eaten,
Their milk milked, barren ! —
Joyless ( a-nanda ) certainly are those worlds
He goes to, who gives such [cows] ! ’

documents.sanskrit:
स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति ।
द्वितीयं तृतीयं त होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति
documents.text:
Then he said to his father : ‘ Papa, to whom will you give
me ? ’ — a second time — a third time.
To him then he said : ‘To Death I give you ! ’

documents.sanskrit:
बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः ।
कि स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाऽद्य करिष्यति
documents.text:
[Naciketas reflects :]
Of many I go as the first.
Of many I go as an intermediate.
What, pray, has Yama (Death) to be done
That he will do with me today ?

documents.sanskrit:
अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथा परे ।
सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः
documents.text:
Look forward, how [fared] the former ones.
Look backward ; so [will] the after ones.
Like grain a mortal ripens !
Like grain he is born hither (a-jayate) again!

documents.sanskrit:
वैश्वानरः प्रविशति अतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान् ।
तस्यैता शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम्
documents.text:
[Voice :]
As fire, enters
A Brahman ( brahmana ) guest into houses.
They make this the quieting thereof: —
Fetch water, Vaivasvata !

documents.sanskrit:
आशाप्रतीक्षे सङ्गत सूनृतां च इष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूश्च सर्वान् ।
एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो यस्यानश्नन्वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे
documents.text:
Hope and expectation, intercourse and pleasantness,
Sacrifices and meritorious deeds, sons and cattle, all —
This he snatches away from the man of little understanding
In whose home a Brahman remains without eating.
Three boons offered to Naciketas
[Death (Yama), returning from a three days’ absence and
finding that Naciketas has not received the hospitality which
is due to a Brahman, says:]

documents.sanskrit:
तिस्रो रात्रीर्यदवात्सीर्गृहे मे अनश्नन् ब्रह्मन्नतिथिर्नमस्यः ।
नमस्तेऽस्तु ब्रह्मन्स्वस्ति मेऽस्तु तस्मात्प्रति त्रीन्वरान्वृणीष्व
documents.text:
Since for three nights thou hast abode in my house
Without eating, O Brahman ( brahman ), a guest to be reverenced,
Reverence be to thee, O Brahman ! Well-being ( svasti ) be
Therefore in return choose three boons !
Naciketas’s first wish : return to an appeased father on earth
[Naciketas :]

documents.sanskrit:
शान्तसङ्कल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माभिमृत्यो ।
त्वत्प्रसृष्टं माऽभिवदेत्प्रतीत एतत् त्रयाणां प्रथम वरं वृणे
documents.text:
With intent appeased, well-minded, with passion departed,
That Gautama toward me may be, O Death ;
That cheerfully he may greet me, when from thee dismissed —
This of the three as boon the first I choose !

documents.sanskrit:
यथा पुरस्ताद्भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः ।
सुख रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युः त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुक्तम्
documents.text:
[Death :]
Cheerful as formerly will he be —
Auddalaki Aruni, from me dismissed.
Happily will he sleep o’ nights, with passion departed,
When he has seen thee from the mouth of Death released.

documents.sanskrit:
स्वर्गे लोके न भयं किञ्चनास्ति न तत्र त्वं न जरया बिभेति ।
उभे तीर्त्वा अशनायापिपासे शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके
documents.text:
[Naciketas:]
.In the heavenly world is no fear whatsoever.
Not there art thou. Not from old age does one fear.
Over both having crossed — hunger, and thirst too —
Gone beyond sorrow, one rejoices in the heaven-world.

documents.sanskrit:
स त्वमग्नि स्वर्ग्यमध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि त्व श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम् ।
स्वर्गलोका अमृतत्वं भजन्त एतद् द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण
documents.text:
Thyself, O Death, understandest the heavenly fire.
Declare it to me who have faith (sraddadhana).
Heaven-world people partake of immortality.
This I choose with boon the second.

documents.sanskrit:
प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन् ।
अनन्तलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्धि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायाम्
documents.text:
[Death :]
To thee I do declare, and do thou learn it of me —
Understanding about the heavenly fire, O Naciketas !
The attainment of the infinite world, likewise too its establishment—
Know thou that as set down in the secret place [of the heart].

documents.sanskrit:
लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्मै या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा ।
स चापि तत्प्रत्यवदद्यथोक्तं अथास्य मृत्युः पुनरेवाह तुष्टः
documents.text:
[Narrative :]
He told him of that fire as the beginning of the world,
What bricks, and how many, and how [built].
And he too repeated that, as it was told.
Then, pleased with him, Death said again —

documents.sanskrit:
तमब्रवीत्प्रीयमाणो महात्मा वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः ।
तवैव नाम्ना भवितायमग्निः सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण
documents.text:
Delighting, the great soul ( mahatman ) said to him: —
[Death resumes :]
A further boon I give thee here today.
By thy name indeed shall this fire be [known].
This multifold garland ( srnka ), too, accept.

documents.sanskrit:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू ।
ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा निचाय्य मा शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति
documents.text:
Having kindled a triple Naciketas-fire, having attained union
with the three,
Performing the triple work, one crosses over birth and death.
By knowing the knower of what is born from Brahma, the
god to be praised,
[And] by revering [him], one goes for ever to this [peace
( santi ).

documents.sanskrit:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा य एवं विद्वाश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् ।
स मृत्युपाशान्पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके
documents.text:
Having kindled a triple Naciketas-fire, having known this triad,
He who knowing thus, builds up the Naciketas-fire —
He, having cast off in advance the bonds of death,
With sorrow overpassed, rejoices in the heaven-world.

documents.sanskrit:
एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण ।
एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासः तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व
documents.text:
This, O Naciketas, is thy heavenly fire,
Which thou didst choose with the second boon.
As thine, indeed, will folks proclaim this fire,
The third boon, Naciketas, choose !

documents.sanskrit:
येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये अस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके ।
एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाऽहं वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः
documents.text:
[Naciketas :]
This doubt that there is in regard to a man deceased :
* He exists,’ say some ; ‘ He exists not,’ say others —
This would I know, instructed by thee !
Of the boons this is boon the third.

documents.sanskrit:
देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा न हि सुविज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः ।
अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम्
documents.text:
[Death :]
Even the gods had doubt as to this of yore !
For truly, it is not easily to be understood. Subtile is this
matter ( dharma ).
Another boon, O Naciketas, choose !
Press me not ! Give up this one for me !

documents.sanskrit:
देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ ।
वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित्
documents.text:
[Naciketas :]
Even the gods had doubt, indeed, as to this,
And thou, O Death, sayest that it is not easily to be understood.
And another declarer of it the like of thee is not to be obtained.
No other boon the equal of it is there at all.

documents.sanskrit:
शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान्वृणीष्वा बहून्पशून् हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान् ।
भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि
documents.text:
[Death :]
Choose centenarian sons and grandsons,
Many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses.
Choose a great abode of earth.
And thyself live as many autumns as thou desirest.

documents.sanskrit:
एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च ।
महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि
documents.text:
This, if thou thinkest an equal boon,
Choose — wealth and long life !
A great one on earth, O Naciketas, be thou.
The enjoyer of thy desires I make thee.

documents.sanskrit:
ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके सर्वान् कामाश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व ।
इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः ।
आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतो मरणं माऽनुप्राक्षीः
documents.text:
Whate’er desires are hard to get in mortal world —
For all desires at pleasure make request.
These lovely maidens with chariots, with lyres —
Such [maidens], indeed, are not obtainable by men —
By these, from me bestowed, be waited on
O Naciketas, question me not regarding dying ( marana )

documents.sanskrit:
श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत् सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः ।
अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते
documents.text:
[Naciketas :]
Ephemeral things! That which is a mortal’s, O End-maker,
Even the vigor (tejas ) of all the powers, they wear away.
Even a whole life is slight indeed.
Thine be the vehicles (vaha) ! Thine be the dance and song!

documents.sanskrit:
न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा ।
जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव
documents.text:
Not with wealth is a man to be satisfied.
Shall we take wealth, if we have seen thee ?
Shall we live so long as thou shalt rule?
— This, in truth, is the boon to be chosen by me.

documents.sanskrit:
अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य जीर्यन्मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् ।
अभिध्यायन्वर्णरतिप्रमोदान् अतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत
documents.text:
When one has come into the presence of undecaying immortals,
What decaying mortal here below that understands,
That meditates upon the pleasures of beauty and delight,
Would delight in a life over-long?

documents.sanskrit:
यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् ।
योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते
documents.text:
This thing whereon they doubt, O Death:
What there is in the great passing-on — tell us that
This boon, that has entered into the hidden —
No other than that does Naciketas choose.

documents.sanskrit: अन्यच्छ्रेयोऽन्यदुतैव प्रेयस्ते उभे नानार्थे पुरुषं सिनीतः । तयोः श्रेय आददानस्य साधु भवति हीयतेऽर्थाद्य उ प्रेयो वृणीते ॥
documents.transliteration: anyachchreyo'nyadutaiva preyaste ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṁ sinītaḥ | tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate'rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte ||
documents.text:
The better ( sreyas ) is one thing, and the pleasanter ( preyas )
quite another.
Both these, of different aim, bind a person.
Of these two, well is it for him who takes the better;
He fails of his aim who chooses the pleasanter.

documents.sanskrit:
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः
तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः ।
श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते
प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते
documents.text:
Both the better and the pleasanter come to a man.
Going all around the two, the wise man discriminates.
The wise man chooses the better, indeed, rather than the
pleasanter.
The stupid man, from getting-and-keeping ( yoga-ksema ), chooses
the pleasanter.

documents.sanskrit:
स त्वं प्रियान्प्रियरूपांश्च कामान्
अभिध्यायन्नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः ।
नैता सृङ्कां वित्तमयीमवाप्तो
यस्यां मज्जन्ति बहवो मनुष्याः
documents.text:
Thou indeed, upon the pleasant and pleasantly appearing
desires
Meditating, hast let them go, O Naciketas.
Thou art not one who has taken that garland of wealth
In which many men sink down.

documents.sanskrit:
दूरमेते विपरीते विषूची
अविद्या या च विद्येति ज्ञाता ।
विद्याभीप्सिनं नचिकेतसं मन्ये
न त्वा कामा बहवोऽलोलुपन्त
documents.text:
Widely opposite and asunder are these two :
Ignorance ( avidya ) and what is known as ‘ knowledge ’ ( vidya ).
I think Naciketas desirous of obtaining knowledge!
Many desires rend thee not.

documents.sanskrit:
अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः
स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः ।
दन्द्रम्यमाणाः परियन्ति मूढा
अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः
documents.text:
Those abiding in the midst of ignorance,
Self-wise, thinking themselves learned,
Running hither and thither, go around deluded,
Like blind men led by one who is himself blind.

documents.sanskrit:
न साम्परायः प्रतिभाति बालं
प्रमाद्यन्तं वित्तमोहेन मूढम् ।
अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी
पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे
documents.text:
The passing-on is not clear to him who is childish,
Heedless, deluded with the delusion of wealth.
Thinking ‘ This is the world ! There is no other ! ’ —
Again and again he comes under my control.

documents.sanskrit:
श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्यः
शृण्वन्तोऽपि बहवो यं न विद्युः ।
आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धा
आश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानुशिष्टः
documents.text:
He who by many is not obtainable even to hear of,
He whom many, even when hearing, know not —
Wonderful is the declarer, proficient the obtainer of Him!
Wonderful the knower, proficiently taught !

documents.sanskrit:
न नरेणावरेण प्रोक्त
एष सुविज्ञेयो बहुधा चिन्त्यमानः ।
अनन्यप्रोक्ते गतिरत्र नास्ति
अणीयान्ह्यतर्क्यमणुप्रमाणात्
documents.text:
Not, when proclaimed by an inferior man, is He
To be well understood, [though] being manifoldly considered.
Unless declared by another, there is no going thither;
For He is inconceivably more subtile than what is of subtile
measure.

documents.sanskrit:
नैषा तर्केण मतिरापनेया
प्रोक्तान्येनैव सुज्ञानाय प्रेष्ठ ।
यां त्वमापः सत्यधृतिर्बतासि
त्वादृङ् नो भूयान्नचिकेतः प्रष्टा
documents.text:
Not by reasoning ( tarka ) is this thought ( mati ) to be attained.
Proclaimed by another, indeed, it is for easy understanding,
dearest friend ( prestha)\ —
This which thou hast attained ! Ah, thou art of true steadfastness !
May there be for us a questioner (prasta) the like of thee,
O Naciketas!
Steadfast renunciation and self-meditation required
[Naciketas :]

documents.sanskrit:
जानाम्यह शेवधिरित्यनित्यं
न ह्यध्रुवैः प्राप्यते हि ध्रुवं तत् ।
ततो मया नाचिकेतश्चितोऽग्निरनित्यैर्द्रव्यैः प्राप्तवानस्मि नित्यम्
documents.text:
I know that what is known as treasure is something inconstant.
For truly, that which is steadfast is not obtained by those
who are unsteadfast.
Therefore the Naciketas-fire has been built up by me,
And with means which are inconstant I have obtained that
which is constant.

documents.sanskrit:
कामस्याप्तिं जगतः प्रतिष्ठां
क्रतोरानन्त्यमभयस्य पारम् ।
स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां
दृष्ट्वा धृत्या धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः
documents.text:
[Death :]
The obtainment of desire, the foundation of the world ( jagat ),
The endlessness of will, the safe shore of fearlessness,
The greatness of praise, the wide extent, the foundation
(having seen *),
Thou, O Naciketas, a wise one, hast with steadfastness let
[these] go !

documents.sanskrit:
तं दुर्दर्शं गूढमनुप्रविष्टं
गुहाहितं गह्वरेष्ठं पुराणम् ।
अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं
मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति
documents.text:
Him who is hard to see, entered into the hidden,
Set in the secret place [of the heart], dwelling in the depth,
primeval —
By considering him as God, through the Yoga-study of what
pertains to self,
The wise man leaves joy and sorrow behind.

documents.sanskrit:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा सम्परिगृह्य मर्त्यः
प्रवृह्य धर्म्यमणुमेतमाप्य ।
स मोदते मोदनीयं हि लब्ध्वा
विवृत सद्म नचिकेतसं मन्ये
documents.text:
Y hen a mortal has heard this and fully comprehended,
Has torn off what is concerned with the right ( dharmya ), and
has taken Him as the subtile,
Then he rejoices, for indeed he has obtained what is to be
rejoiced in.
I regard Naciketas a dwelling open [for Atman].

documents.sanskrit:
अन्यत्र धर्मादन्यत्राधर्मादन्यत्रास्मात्कृताकृतात् ।
अन्यत्र भूताच्च भव्याच्च
यत्तत्पश्यसि तद्वद
documents.text:
Apart from the right ( dharma ) and apart from the unright
( a-dharma ),
Apart from both what has been done and what has not been
done here,
Apart from what has been and what is to be —
What thou seest as that, speak that !
[Naciketas being unable to mention that absolutely unqualified object, Death continues to explain :]

documents.sanskrit:
सर्वे वेदा यत्पदमामनन्ति
तपांसि सर्वाणि च यद्वदन्ति ।
यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति
तत्ते पदं सङ्ग्रहेण ब्रवीम्योमित्येतत्
documents.text:
The word which all the Vedas rehearse,
And which all austerities proclaim,
Desiring which men live the life of religious studentship
( brahmacarya ) —
That word to thee I briefly declare.
That is Om !

documents.sanskrit:
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं परम् ।
एतद्ध्येवाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत्
documents.text:
That syllable, truly, indeed, is Brahma !
That syllable indeed is the supreme !
Knowing that syllable, truly, indeed,
Whatever one desires is his !

documents.sanskrit:
एतदालम्बनँ श्रेष्ठमेतदालम्बनं परम् ।
एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
documents.text:
That is the best support.
That is the supreme support.
Knowing that support,
One becomes happy in the Brahma-world.

documents.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा विपश्चिन्नायं कुतश्चिन्न बभूव कश्चित् ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे
documents.text:
The wise one [i. e. the soul, the atman, the self] is not born,
nor dies.
This one has not come from anywhere, has not become anyone.
Unborn, constant, eternal, primeval, this one
Is not slain when the body is slain.

documents.sanskrit:
हन्ता चेन्मन्यते हन्तुँ हतश्चेन्मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायँ हन्ति न हन्यते
documents.text:
If the slayer think to slay.
If the slain think himself slain,
Both these understand not.
This one slays not, nor is slain.

documents.sanskrit:
अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयानात्माऽस्य जन्तोर्निहितो गुहायाम् ।
तमक्रतुः पश्यति वीतशोको
धातुप्रसादान्महिमानमात्मनः
documents.text:
More minute than the minute, greater than the great
Is the Soul (Atman) that is set in the heart of a creature here.
One who is without the active will ( a-kratu ) beholds Him,
and becomes freed from sorrow —
When through the grace ( prasada ) of the Creator ( dhatr ) he
beholds the greatness of the Soul (Atman).

documents.sanskrit:
आसीनो दूरं व्रजति शयानो याति सर्वतः ।
कस्तं मदामदं देवं मदन्यो ज्ञातुमर्हति
documents.text:
Sitting, he proceeds afar;
Lying, he goes everywhere.
Who else than I (mad) is able to know
The god ( deva ) who rejoices and rejoices not ( madamada )?

documents.sanskrit:
अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
documents.text:
Him who is the bodiless among bodies,
Stable among the unstable,
The great, all-pervading Soul (Atman) —
On recognizing Him, the wise man sorrows not.

documents.sanskrit:
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो
न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।
यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्य
स्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनू स्वाम्
documents.text:
This Soul (Atman) is not to be obtained by instruction,
Nor by intellect, nor by much learning.
He is to be obtained only by the one whom He chooses ;
To such a one that Soul (Atman) reveals his own person
( tanum svam ).

documents.sanskrit:
नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः ।
नाशान्तमानसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात्
documents.text:
Not he who has not ceased from bad conduct,
Not he who is not tranquil, not he who is not composed,
Not he who is not of peaceful mind
Can obtain Him by intelligence ( prajna ).

documents.sanskrit:
यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः ।
मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः
documents.text:
He for whom the priesthood ( brahman ) and the nobility
( ksatra )
Both are as food,
And death is as a sauce —
Who really knows where He is?

documents.sanskrit:
ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे ।
छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः
documents.text:
There are two that drink of righteousness ( rta ) in the world
of good deeds ;
Both are entered into the secret place [of the heart], and in
the highest upper sphere.
Brahma-knowers speak of them as ‘ light ’ and ‘ shade,’
And so do householders who maintain the five sacrificial fires,
and those too who perform the triple Naciketas-fire.

documents.sanskrit:
यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत्परम् ।
अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं नाचिकेतं शकेमहि
documents.text:
This which is the bridge for those who sacrifice,
And which is the highest imperishable Brahma
For those who seek to cross over to the fearless farther
shore —
The Naciketas-fire may we master !

documents.sanskrit:
आत्मानं रथितं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु ।
बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च
documents.text:
Know thou the soul ( atman , self) as riding in a chariot.
The body as the chariot.
Know thou the intellect ( buddhi ) as the chariot-driver,
And the mind ( manas ) as the reins.

documents.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयां स्तेषु गोचरान् ।
आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः
documents.text:
The senses ( indriya ), they say, are the horses ;
The objects of sense, what they range over.
The self combined with senses and mind
Wise men call ‘ the enjoyer ’ ( bhoktr ).

documents.sanskrit:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः
documents.text:
He who has not understanding ( a-vijnana ),
Whose mind is not constantly held firm —
His senses are uncontrolled,
Like the vicious horses of a chariot-driver.

documents.sanskrit:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा ।
तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः
documents.text:
He, however, who has understanding,
Whose mind is constantly held firm —
His senses are under control,
Like the good horses of a chariot-driver.

documents.sanskrit:
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः ।
न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति
documents.text:
He, however, who has not understanding,
Who is unmindful and ever impure,
Reaches not the goal.
But goes on to transmigration ( samsara ).

documents.sanskrit:
यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः ।
स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते
documents.text:
He, however, who has understanding,
Who is mindful and ever pure,
Reaches the goal
From which he is born no more.

documents.sanskrit:
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनः प्रग्रहवान्नरः ।
सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम्
documents.text:
He, however, who has the understanding of a chariot- driver,
A man who reins in his mind —
He reaches the end of his journey,
That highest place of Vishnu.

documents.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः
documents.text:
Higher than the senses are the objects of sense.
Higher than the objects of sense is the mind ( manas ) ;
And higher than the mind is the intellect ( buddhi ).
Higher than the intellect is the Great Self (Atman).

documents.sanskrit:
महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः ।
पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः
documents.text:
Higher than the Great is the Unmanifest ( avyakta ).
Higher than the Unmanifest is the Person.
Higher than the Person there is nothing at all.
That is the goal. That is the highest course.

documents.sanskrit:
एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽत्मा न प्रकाशते ।
दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः
documents.text:
Though He is hidden in all things,
That Soul (Atman, Self) shines not forth.
But he is seen by subtle seers
With superior, subtle intellect.

documents.sanskrit:
यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि ।
ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि
documents.text:
An intelligent man should suppress his speech and his mind.
The latter he should suppress in the Understanding-Self
(jnana atman).
The understanding he should suppress in the Great Self
[= buddhi, intellect].
That he should suppress in the Tranquil Self ( santa atman).

documents.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥
documents.transliteration: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varānnibodhata | kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṁ pathastatkavayo vadanti ||
documents.text:
Arise ye ! Awake ye !
Obtain your boons and understand them !
A sharpened edge of a razor, hard to traverse,
A difficult path is this — poets ( kavi ) declare !

documents.sanskrit:
अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथाऽरसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् ।
अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तं मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते
documents.text:
What is soundless, touchless, formless, imperishable,
Likewise tasteless, constant, odorless,
Without beginning, without end, higher than the great, stable —
By discerning That, one is liberated from the mouth of death.

documents.sanskrit:
नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तँ सनातनम् ।
उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते
documents.text:
The Naciketas tale,
Death’s immemorial teaching —
By declaring and hearing this, a wise man
Is magnified in the Brahma-world.

documents.sanskrit:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद् ब्रह्मसंसदि ।
प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते । तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति
documents.text:
If one recites this supreme secret
In an assembly of Brahmans,
Or at a time of the ceremony for the dead, devoutly —
That makes for immortality !
— That makes for immortality!

documents.sanskrit:
पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् ।
कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन्
documents.text:
The Self-existent ( svayambhu ) pierced the openings [of the
senses] outward ;
Therefore one looks outward, not within himself ( antaratman ).
A certain wise man, while seeking immortality,
Introspectively beheld the Soul (Atman) face to face.

documents.sanskrit:
पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् ।
अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा
ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते
documents.text:
The childish go after outward pleasures ;
They walk into the net of widespread death.
But the wise, knowing immortality,
Seek not the stable among things which are unstable here.

documents.sanskrit:
येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शांश्च मैथुनान् ।
एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
That by which [one discerns] form, taste, smell,
Sound, and mutual touches —
It is with That indeed that one discerns.
What is there left over here !
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
documents.text:
By recognizing as the great pervading Soul (Atman)
That whereby one perceives both
The sleeping state and the waking state,
The wise man sorrows not.

documents.sanskrit:
य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् ।
ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
He who knows this experiencer
As the living Soul (Atman) near at hand,
Lord of what has been and of what is to be —
He does not shrink away from Him.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
He who was born of old from austerity (/ apas ),
Was born of old from the waters,
Who stands entered into the secret place [of the heart].
Who looked forth through beings —
This,' verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
या प्राणेन सम्भवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
She who arises with life (prana),
Aditi (Infinity), maker of divinity,
Who stands entered into the secret place [of the heart],
Who was born forth through beings —
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
अरण्योर्निर्हितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः ।
दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
Fire (Agni), the all-knower (Jatavedas ), hidden away in the
two fire-sticks
Like the embryo well borne by pregnant women,
Worthy to be worshiped day by day
By watchful men with oblations —
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
यतश्चोदेति सूर्यः अस्तं यत्र च गच्छति ।
तं देवाः सर्वे अर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
Whence the sun rises,
And where it goes to rest —
On Him all the gods are founded ;
And no one ever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति
documents.text:
Whatever is here, that is there.
What is there, that again is here.
He obtains death after death
Who seems to see a difference here.

documents.sanskrit:
मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति
documents.text:
By the mind, indeed, is this [realization] to be attained : —
There is no difference here at all !
He goes from death to death
Who seems to see a difference here.

documents.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति ।
ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb
Stands in the midst of one’s self ( atman ),
Lord of what has been and of what is to be.
One does not shrink away from Him.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः ।
ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb,
Like a light without smoke,
Lord of what has been and what is to be.
He alone is today, and tomorrow too.

documents.sanskrit:
यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति ।
एवं धर्मान् पृथक्पश्यंस्तानेवानुविधावति
documents.text:
As water rained upon rough ground
Runs to waste among the hills,
So he who sees qualities ( dharma ) separately,
Runs to waste after them.

documents.sanskrit:
यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति ।
एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम
documents.text:
As pure water poured forth into pure
Becomes the very same,
So becomes the soul ( atman ), O Gautama,
Of the seer (muni) who has understanding.

documents.sanskrit:
पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः ।
अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
By ruling over the eleven-gated citadel
Of the Unborn, the Un-crooked-minded one,
One sorrows not.
But when liberated [from the body], he is liberated indeed.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
हसः शुचिषद्वसुरान्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।
नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत्
documents.text:
The swan [i. e. sun] in the clear, the Vasu in the atmosphere,
The priest by the altar, the guest in the house,
In man, in broad space, in the right ( rta ), in the sky,
Born in water, born in cattle, born in the right, born in rock,
is the Right, the Great !

documents.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयति अपानं प्रत्यगस्यति ।
मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते
documents.text:
Upwards the out-breath ( prana ) he leadeth.
The in-breath ( apana ) inwards he casts.
The dwarf who is seated in the middle
All the gods ( deva ) reverence !

documents.sanskrit:
अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः ।
देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
When this incorporate one that stands in the body
Is dissolved,
And is released from the body,
What is there left over here ?
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन ।
इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ
documents.text:
Not by the out-breath (prana) and the in-breath ( apana )
Doth any mortal whatsoever live.
But by another do men live —
Even That whereon both these depend.

documents.sanskrit:
हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम
documents.text:
Come ! I will declare this to you :
The hidden, eternal Brahma;
And how, after it reaches death,
The soul (atman) fares, O Gautama !

documents.sanskrit:
योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः ।
स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम्
documents.text:
Some go into a womb
For the embodiment of a corporeal being.
Others go into a stationary thing
According to their deeds ( karman ), according to their
knowledge.

documents.sanskrit:
य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
He who is awake in those that sleep,
The Person who fashions desire after desire —
That indeed is the Pure. That is Brahma.
That indeed is called the Immortal.
On it all the worlds do rest ;
And no one soever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च
documents.text:
As the one fire has entered the world
And becomes corresponding in form to every form,
So the one Inner Soul (Atman) of all things
Is corresponding in form to every form, and yet is outside.

documents.sanskrit:
वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च
documents.text:
As the one wind has entered the world
And becomes corresponding in form to every form,
So the one Inner Soul of all things
Is corresponding in form to every form, and yet is outside.

documents.sanskrit:
सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुर्न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः
documents.text:
As the sun, the eye of the whole world,
Is not sullied by the external faults of the eyes,
So the one Inner Soul of all things
Is not sullied by the evil in the world, being external to it.

documents.sanskrit:
एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम्
documents.text:
The Inner Soul ( antaratman ) of all things, the One Controller,
Who makes his one form manifold —
The wise who perceive Him as standing in oneself,
They, and no others, have eternal happiness !

documents.sanskrit:
नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानामेको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीरा
स्तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम्
documents.text:
Him who is the constant among the inconstant, the intelligent
among intelligences,
The One among many, who grants desires —
The wise who perceive Him as standing in oneself,
They, and no others, have eternal peace !

documents.sanskrit:
तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् ।
कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा
documents.text:
‘This is it!’ — thus they recognize
The highest, indescribable happiness.
How, now, shall I understand ‘ this ’ ?
Does it shine [of itself] or does it shine in reflection?

documents.sanskrit:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं
नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं
तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति
documents.text:
The sun shines not there, nor the moon and stars,
These lightnings shine not, much less this (earthly) fire !
After Him, as He shines, doth everything shine,
This whole world is illumined with His light.

documents.sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शातख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत्
documents.text:
Its root is above, its branches below —
This eternal fig-tree !
That (root) indeed is the Pure. That is Brahma.
That indeed is called the Immortal.
On it all the worlds do rest,
And no one soever goes beyond it.
This, verily, is That !

documents.sanskrit:
यदिदं किंच जगत्सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् ।
महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति
documents.text:
This whole world, whatever there is,
Was created from and moves in Life (prana).
The great fear, the upraised thunderbolt —
They who know That, become immortal.

documents.sanskrit:
भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः ।
भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः
documents.text:
From fear of Him fire (Agni) doth burn.
From fear the sun (Surya) gives forth heat.
From fear both Indra and Wind (Vayu),
And Death (Mrityu) as fifth, do speed along.
Degrees of perception of the Soul (Atman).

documents.sanskrit:
इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्शरीरस्य विस्रसः ।
ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते
documents.text:
If one has been able to perceive [Him] here on earth
Before the dissolution of the body,
According to that [knowledge] he becomes fitted
For embodiment in the world-creations.

documents.sanskrit:
यथादर्शे तथाऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके ।
यथाऽप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके
च्छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके

इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् ।
पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति
documents.text:
The separate nature of the senses,
And that their arising and setting
Is of things that come into being apart [from himself],
The wise man recognizes, and sorrows not.

documents.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम्

अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च ।
यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति
documents.text:
Higher than the Unmanifest, however, is the Person
(Purusha),
All-pervading and without any mark ( a-linga ) whatever.
Knowing which, a man is liberated
And goes to immortality.

documents.sanskrit:
न सन्दृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य
न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् ।
हृदा मनीषा मनसाऽभिक्लृप्तो
य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति
documents.text:
His form is not to be beheld.
No one soever sees Him with the eye.
He is framed by the heart, by the thought, by the mind.
They who know That become immortal.

documents.sanskrit:
यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह ।
बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टति तामाहुः परमां गतिम्
documents.text:
When cease the five
[Sense-]knowledges, together with the mind ( manas ),
And the intellect ( buddhi ) stirs not —
That, they say, is the highest course.

documents.sanskrit:
तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् ।
अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ
documents.text:
This they consider as Yoga —
The firm holding back of the senses.
Then one becomes undistracted.
Yoga, truly, is the origin and the end.

documents.sanskrit:
नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा ।
अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते
documents.text:
Not by speech, not by mind,
Not by sight can He be apprehended.
How can He be comprehended
Otherwise than by one’s saying ‘ He is ’ ?

documents.sanskrit:
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः ।
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति
documents.text:
He can indeed be comprehended by the thought ‘He is’
(asti)
And by [admitting] the real nature of both [his comprehensibility and his incomprehensibility].
When he has been comprehended by the thought ‘He is’
His real nature manifests itself.

documents.sanskrit:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते
documents.text:
When are liberated all
The desires that lodge in one’s heart,
Then a mortal becomes immortal !
Therein he reaches Brahma !

documents.sanskrit:
यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम्
documents.text:
When are cut all
The knots of the heart here on earth,
Then a mortal becomes immortal !
— Thus far is the instruction.

documents.sanskrit:
शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका ।
तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति
विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति
documents.text:
There are a hundred and one arteries of the heart.
One of these passes up to the crown of the head.
Going up by it, one goes to immortality.
The others are for departing in various directions.

documents.sanskrit:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा
सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः ।
तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण ।
तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति
documents.text:
A Person of the measure of a thumb is the inner soul
( antaratman ),
Ever seated in the heart of creatures.
Him one should draw out from one’s own body
Like an arrow-shaft out from a reed, with firmness.
Him one should know as the Pure, the Immortal —
Yea, Him one should know as the Pure, the Immortal.

documents.sanskrit:
मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् ।
ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्युरन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव
documents.text:
Then Naciketas, having received this knowledge
Declared by Death, and the entire rule of Yoga,
Attained Brahma and became free from passion, free from death ;
And so may any other who knows this in regard to the Soul
(Atman).

documents.sanskrit: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद्वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश्चक्षुरतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
documents.transliteration: śrotrasya śrotraṁ manaso mano yadvāco ha vācaṁ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaścakṣuratimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ||
documents.text: It is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, the life of life, and the eye of the eye. The wise, freed from sense-perceptions, on leaving this world become immortal.

documents.sanskrit: केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः । केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदन्ति चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥
documents.transliteration: keneṣitaṁ patati preṣitaṁ manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ | keneṣitāṁ vācamimāṁ vadanti cakṣuḥ śrotraṁ ka u devo yunakti ||
documents.text: By whose will directed does the mind fly forth? By whose command does the first breath move? By whose will do people utter speech? What god directs the eye and ear?

documents.sanskrit: न तत्र चक्षुर्गच्छति न वाग्गच्छति नो मनो न विद्मो न विजानीमो यथैतदनुशिष्यात् ।
documents.transliteration: na tatra cakṣurgacchati na vāggacchati no mano na vidmo na vijānīmo yathaitadanuśiṣyāt |
documents.text: There the eye does not go, nor speech, nor the mind. We do not know, we do not understand, how anyone can teach this.

documents.sanskrit: यदि मन्यसे सुवेदेति दभ्रमेवापि नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपम् । यदस्य त्वं यदस्य देवेष्वथ नु मीमांस्यमेव ते मन्ये विदितम् ॥
documents.transliteration: yadi manyase suvedeti dabhramevāpi nūnaṁ tvaṁ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam | yadasya tvaṁ yadasya deveṣvatha nu mīmāṁsyameva te manye viditam ||
documents.text: If you think 'I know Brahman well,' then surely you know very little of Its form. What you know of Brahman in yourself, what you know in the gods — that alone is worth contemplating.

documents.sanskrit: नाहं मन्ये सुवेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च । यो नस्तद्वेद तद्वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ॥
documents.transliteration: nāhaṁ manye suvedeti no na vedeti veda ca | yo nastadveda tadveda no na vedeti veda ca ||
documents.text: I do not think that I know Brahman well, nor do I think that I do not know It. He among us who knows what is meant by 'I neither know nor do I not know' — he knows Brahman.

documents.sanskrit: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त ।
documents.transliteration: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta |
documents.text: Brahman won a victory for the gods. The gods became elated in the victory of Brahman.

documents.sanskrit: ओमित्येतदक्षरमिदं सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानं भूतं भवद्भविष्यदिति सर्वमोंकार एव । यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योंकार एव ॥
documents.transliteration: omityetadakṣaramidaṁ sarvaṁ tasyopavyākhyānaṁ bhūtaṁ bhavadbhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṁkāra eva | yaccānyat trikālātītaṁ tadapyoṁkāra eva ||
documents.text:
Om ! — This syllable is this whole world.

Its further explanation is : —

The past, the present, the future — everything is just the
word Om.

And whatever else that transcends threefold time 2 — that, too,
is just the word Om.

documents.sanskrit: सर्वं ह्येतद्ब्रह्मायमात्मा ब्रह्म सोऽयमात्मा चतुष्पात् ।
documents.transliteration: sarvaṁ hyetadbrahm āyamātmā brahma so'yamātmā catuṣpāt |
documents.text:
For truly, everything here is Brahma ; this self ( dtman ) is
Brahma. This same self has four fourths.

documents.sanskrit: जागरितस्थानो बहिष्प्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः ॥
documents.transliteration: jāgaritasthāno bahiṣprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṁśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhugvaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
documents.text:
The waking state {jagarita-sthana), outwardly cognitive,
having seven limbs,3 having nineteen mouths,4 enjoying the
gross ( stJiula-bhuj ), the Common-to-all-men ( vaisvanara ), is
the first fourth.

documents.sanskrit: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः ॥
documents.transliteration: svapnasthāno'ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṁśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
documents.text:
The dreaming state ( svapna-sthana ), inwardly cognitive,
having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the
exquisite ( pravivikta-bhuj ), the Brilliant ( taijasa ), is the second
fourth.

documents.sanskrit: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत्सुषुप्तम् ।
documents.transliteration: yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṁ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṁ paśyati tatssuṣuptam |
documents.text:
If one asleep desires no desire whatsoever, sees no dream
whatsoever.1 2 that is deep sleep (sitsupta).

The deep-sleep state ( susnpta-st/iana. ), unified (eki-bhuta)?
just (eva.) a cognition-mass ( prajnana-ghana ),3 consisting of
bliss ( ananda-maya ),4 enjoying bliss (ananda-b/mj) , whose
mouth is thought (cetas-), the Cognitional ( prdjiia ), is the
third fourth.

documents.sanskrit: एष सर्वेश्वरः एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्यप्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम्
documents.text:
This is the lord of all (sarvesvai'a).5 This is the all-
knowing ( sarva-jna)P This is the inner controller ( aiitar -
yamin ).7 This is the source ( yotti ) 8 of all, for this is the
origin and the end ( prabhavapyayau) 9 of beings.

documents.sanskrit: नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् ।
documents.transliteration: nāntaḥprajñaṁ na bahiṣprajñaṁ nobhayataḥprajñaṁ na prajñānaghanaṁ na prajñaṁ nāprajñam |
documents.text:
Not inwardly cognitive {antah-prajna), not outwardly
cognitive ( bahih-prajiia ), not both-wise cognitive ( iibhayatah -
prajna), not a cognition-mass ( prajuana-gJiana), not cognitive
(pj'ajiia), not non-cognitive ( a-prajiia ), unseen (a-drsta), with
which there can be no dealing ( a-zyavahdrya ), ungraspable (a-
grahya ), having no distinctive mark (a-laksatia), non-thinkable
( a-cintya ), that cannot be designated (a-vyapadcsya) ,the essence
of the assurance of which is the state of being one with the
Self10 (ekdtinya-pratyaya-sara), the cessation of development
( prapancopasama ), tranquil (santa)> benign (siva), without a
second ( a-dvaita ) — [such] they think is the fourth.11 He is
the Self (Atman). He should be discerned.

documents.sanskrit: सोऽयमात्माध्यक्षरमोङ्करोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादाअकार उकारो मकार इति
documents.text:
This is the Self with regard to the word Oju, with
regard to its elements. The elements ( matra ) are the fourths ;

documents.sanskrit: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद्वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
documents.text:
The waking state, the Common-to-all-mcn, is the letter a ,
the first element, from apli (‘ obtaining ’) or from adimatvd
(‘ being first ’).

He obtains, verily, indeed, all desires, he becomes first — he
who knows this.

documents.sanskrit: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षात्उभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवतिनास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद
documents.text:
The sleeping state, the Brilliant, is the letter u, the
second element, from utkarsa (‘ exaltation ’) or from ubhayatvd
(‘ intermediateness ’).

He exalts, verily, indeed, the continuity of knowledge ;
and he becomes equal 3 ( samana ) ; no one ignorant of Brahma
is born in the family of him who knows this.

documents.sanskrit: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वामिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
documents.text:
The deep- sleep state, the Cognitional, is the letter in,
the third element, from miti (‘erecting’) or from apitp
(■ immerging ’).

He, verily, indeed, erects ( minoti ) this whole world,4 and he
becomes its immerging — he who knows this.

documents.sanskrit: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैतएवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद
documents.text:
The fourth is without an element, with which there can
be no dealing, the cessation of development, benign, without a
second.

Thus Om is the Self (Atman) indeed.

He who knows this, with his self enters the Self — yea, he
who knows this!

documents.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ताभुवनस्य गोप्ता ।
स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह
documents.text:
Brahma arose as the first of the gods —
The maker of all, the protector of the world.
He told the knowledge of Brahma ( brahma-vidya ), the foundation of all knowledge,
To Atharva[n], his eldest son.

documents.sanskrit:
अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माऽथर्वा तां पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम् ।
स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवाहाय प्राह भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम्
documents.text:
What Brahma taught to Atharvan,
Even that knowledge of Brahma, Atharvan told in ancient
time to Angir.
He told it to Bharadvaja Satyavaha;
Bharadvaja, to Angiras — both the higher and the lower [knowledge].

documents.sanskrit:
शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ
कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति
documents.text:
Saunaka, verily, indeed, a great householder, approached
Angiras according to rule, and asked : ‘ Through understanding of what, pray, does all this world become understood, Sir?’

documents.sanskrit:
तस्मै स होवाच । द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म
यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च
documents.text:
To him then he said : ‘There are two knowledges to be
known — as indeed the knowers of Brahma are wont to say:
a higher (para) and also a lower (apara).

documents.sanskrit:
तत्रापरा, ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति ।
अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते
documents.text:
Of these, the lower is the Rig-Veda, the Yajur-Veda, the
Sama-Veda, the Atharva-Veda,
Pronunciation (siksa), Ritual ( kalpa ), Grammar ( vyakarana ),
Definition ( nirukta ), Metrics ( chandas ), and Astrology
(jyotisa)
Now, the higher is that whereby that Imperishable ( aksara )
is apprehended.

documents.sanskrit:
यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्णमचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम् ।
नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः
documents.text:
That which is invisible, ungraspable, without family, without
caste ( a-varna ) —
Without sight or hearing is It, without hand or foot,
Eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, exceedingly subtile;
That is the Imperishable, which the wise j perceive as the
source of beings.

documents.sanskrit:
यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति ।
यथा सतः पुरुषात्केशलोमानि तथाऽक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम्
documents.text:
As a spider emits and draws in [its thread],
As herbs arise on the earth,
As the hairs of the head and body from a living person,
So from the Imperishable arises everything here.

documents.sanskrit:
तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते ।
अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम्
documents.text:
By austerity ( tapas ) Brahma becomes built up.
From that, food is produced;
From food — life-breath, mind, truth,
The worlds, immortality too in works.

documents.sanskrit:
यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः ।
तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायाते
documents.text:
He who is all-knowing, all- wise,
Whose austerity consists of knowledge —
From Him are produced the Brahma here,
[Namely] name and form, and food.

documents.sanskrit:
तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा संततानि ।
तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके
documents.text:
This is the truth : —
The works which the sages ( kavi ) saw in the sacred sayings
( mantra , i.e. Vedic hymns)
Are manifoldly spread forth in the triad [of the Vedas].
Follow them ( acaratha ) constantly, ye lovers of truth ( satya-kama ) !
This is your path to the world of good deeds.

documents.sanskrit:
यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने ।
तदाऽऽज्यभागावन्तरेणाऽऽहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत्
documents.text:
When the flame flickers,
After the oblation fire has been kindled,
Then, between the two portions of melted butter, his oblations
One should throw — an offering made with faith ( sraddha ).

documents.sanskrit:
यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमासमचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितं च ।
अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुतमासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान्हिनस्ति
documents.text:
If one’s Agnihotra sacrifice is not followed by the sacrifice of the new moon and of the full moon, by the four-months
sacrifice, by the harvest sacrifice, if it is unattended by guests,
or not offered at all, or without the ceremony to all the gods,
or not according to rule, it destroys his seven worlds.

documents.sanskrit:
काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा ।
स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः
documents.text:
The Black (kali), and the Terrible, and the Swift-as-Thought,
The Very-red, and the Very-smoky-colored,
The Scintillating, and the All-formed, divine one,
Are the seven so-called flickering tongues [of flame].

documents.sanskrit:
एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् ।
तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः
documents.text:
If one performs sacrifices when these are shining,
Offering the oblations at the proper time, too,
These (flames) as rays of the sun lead him
To where is resident the one lord (pati) of the gods.

documents.sanskrit:
एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति ।
प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः
documents.text:
Saying to him “ Come Come ! ” the splendid offerings
Carry the sacrificer with the rays of the sun,
Addressing pleasant speech, praising, and saying :
“ This is your meritorious ( punya ) Brahma-world, gained by
good works.”

documents.sanskrit:
प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म ।
एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति
documents.text:
Unsafe boats, however, are these sacrificial forms,
The eighteen, in which is expressed the lower work.
The fools who approve that as the better,
Go again to old age and death.

documents.sanskrit:
अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितं मन्यमानाः ।
जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः
documents.text:
Those abiding in the midst of ignorance,
Self-wise, thinking themselves learned,
Hard smitten, go around deluded,
Like blind men led by one who is himself blind.

documents.sanskrit:
अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमानाः वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः ।
यत्कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात्तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते
documents.text:
Manifoldly living in ignorance,
They think to themselves, childishly : “ We have accomplished
our aim”
Since doers of deeds ( karmin ) do not understand, because of
passion ( raga ),
Therefore, when their worlds are exhausted, they sink down
wretched.

documents.sanskrit:
इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः ।
नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति
documents.text:
Thinking sacrifice and merit is the chiefest thing,
Naught better do they know — deluded !
Having had enjoyment on the top of the heaven won by good
works,
They re-enter this world, or a lower.

documents.sanskrit:
तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्ष्यचर्यां चरन्तः ।
सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा
documents.text:
They who practise austerity ( tapas ) and faith ( sraddha ) in the
forest,
The peaceful ( santa ) knowers who live on alms,
Depart passionless ( vi-raga ) through the door of the sun,
To where is that immortal Person (Purusha), e’en the imperishable Spirit (Atman).

documents.sanskrit:
परीक्ष्य लोकान्कर्मचितान्ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन ।
तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम्
documents.text:
Having scrutinized the worlds that are built up by work, a
Brahman
Should arrive at indifference. The [world] that was not made
is not [won] by what is done.
For the sake of this knowledge let him go, fuel in hand,
To a spiritual teacher (guru) who is learned in the scriptures
and established on Brahma.

documents.sanskrit:
तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक् प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय ।
येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच तां तत्त्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम्
documents.text:
Such a knowing [teacher], unto one who has approached
properly,
Whose thought is tranquilized, who has reached peace,
Teaches in its very truth that knowledge of Brahma
Whereby one knows the Imperishable, the Person, the True.

documents.sanskrit:
तदेतत्सत्यं यथा सुदीप्तात् पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः ।
तथाऽक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापि यन्ति
documents.text:
This is the truth : —
As, from a well-blazing fire, sparks
By the thousand issue forth of like form,
So from the Imperishable, my friend, beings manifold
Are produced, and thither also go.

documents.sanskrit:
दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः ।
अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात्परतः परः
documents.text:
Heavenly ( divya ), formless ( a-murtta ) is the Person (Purusha).
He is without and within, unborn,
Breathless ( a-prana ), mindless (a-manas), pure ( subhra ),
Higher than the high Imperishable.

documents.sanskrit:
एतस्माज्जायते प्राणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च ।
खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी
documents.text:
From Him is produced breath (prana),
Mind ( manas ), and all the senses ( indriya ),
Space (kha), wind, light, water,
And earth, the supporter of all.

documents.sanskrit:
अग्नीर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग् विवृताश्च वेदाः ।
वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा

तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् ।
पुमान् रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात्सम्प्रसूताः
documents.text:
From Him [proceeds] fire, whose fuel is the sun ;
From the moon (Soma), rain ; herbs, on the earth.
The male pours seed in the female.
Many creatures are produced from the Person (Purusha).

documents.sanskrit:
तस्मादृचः साम यजूषि दीक्षा यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च ।
संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः
documents.text:
From Him the Rig Verses, the Saman Chant, the sacrificial
formulas (yajus), the initiation rite (diksa).
And all the sacrifices, ceremonies, and sacrificial gifts ( daksina ),
The year too, and the sacrificer, the worlds
Where the moon (Soma) shines brightly, and where the sun.

documents.sanskrit:
तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा सम्प्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि ।
प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च
documents.text:
From Him, too, gods are manifoldly produced,
The celestials (Sadhyas), men, cattle, birds,
The in-breath and the out-breath ( pranapanau ), rice and
barley, austerity (/ apas ),
Faith ( sraddha ), truth, chastity, and the law ( vidhi ).

documents.sanskrit:
सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात्सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः ।
सप्तेमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त
documents.text:
From Him come forth the seven life-breaths ( prana ),
The seven flames, their fuel, the seven oblations,
These seven worlds, wherein do move
The life-breaths that dwell in the secret place [of the heart],
placed seven and seven.

documents.sanskrit:
अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वे अस्मात्स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः ।
अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा
documents.text:
From Him, the seas and the mountains all.
From Him roll rivers of every kind.
And from Him all herbs, the essence, too,
Whereby that Inner Soul (antaratman) dwells in beings.

documents.sanskrit:
पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम् ।
एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य
documents.text:
The Person (Purusha) himself is everything here:
Work ( karman ) and austerity (tapas) and Brahma, beyond
death.
He who knows That, set in the secret place [of the heart] —
He here on earth, my friend, rends asunder the knot of ignorance.

documents.sanskrit:
आविः संनिहितं गुहाचरं नाम महत्पदमत्रैतत्समर्पितम् ।
एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम्
documents.text:
Manifest, [yet] hidden; called ‘Moving-in-secret’;
The great abode! Therein is placed that
Which moves and breathes and winks.
What that is, know as Being (sad) and Non-being ( a-sad ),
As the object of desire, higher than understanding,
As what is the best of creatures !

documents.sanskrit:
यदर्चिमद्यदणुभ्योऽणु च यस्मिंल्लोका निहिता लोकिनश्च ।
तदेतदक्षरं ब्रह्म स प्राणस्तदु वाङ्मनः तदेतत्सत्यं तदमृतं तद्वेद्धव्यं सोम्य विद्धि
documents.text:
That which is flaming, which is subtler than the subtle,
On which the worlds are set, and their inhabitants —
That is the imperishable Brahma.
It is life (prana), and It is speech and mind.
That is the real. It is immortal.
It is [a mark] to be penetrated. Penetrate It, my friend!

documents.sanskrit:
धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं शरं ह्युपासानिशितं सन्दधीत ।
आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि
documents.text:
Taking as a bow the great weapon of the Upanishad,
One should put upon it an arrow sharpened by meditation.
Stretching it with a thought directed to the essence of That,
Penetrate that Imperishable as the mark, my friend.

documents.sanskrit:
प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते ।
अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत्
documents.text:
The mystic syllable Om (pranava) is the bow. The arrow
is the soul (atman).
Brahma is said to be the mark ( laksya ).
By the undistracted man is It to be penetrated.
One should come to be in It, as the arrow [in the mark].

documents.sanskrit:
यस्मिन्द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः ।
तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः
documents.text:
He on whom the sky, the earth, and the atmosphere
Are woven, and the mind, together with all the life-breaths
(prana),
Him alone know as the one Soul (Atman). Other
Words dismiss. He is the bridge to immortality.

documents.sanskrit:
अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः। स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः ।
ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात्
documents.text:
Where the arteries are brought together
Like the spokes in the hub of a wheel —
Therein he moves about,
Becoming manifold.
Om ! — Thus meditate upon the Soul (Atman).
Success to you in crossing to the farther shore beyond darkness!

documents.sanskrit:
यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्यैष महिमा भुवि । दिव्ये ब्रह्मपुरे ह्येष व्योमन्यात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
मनोमयः प्राणशरीरनेता
प्रतिष्ठितोऽन्ने हृदयं सन्निधाय ।
तद्विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीरा
आनन्दरूपममृतं यद्विभाति
documents.text:
He who is all-knowing, all-wise,
Whose is this greatness on the earth —
He is in the divine Brahma city
And in the heaven established ! The Soul (Atman) !
Consisting of mind, leader of the life-breaths and of the
body,
He is established on food, controlling the heart.
By this knowledge the wise perceive
The blissful Immortal that gleams forth.

documents.sanskrit:
भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः ।
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे
documents.text:
The knot of the heart is loosened,
All doubts are cut off,
And one’s deeds ( karman ) cease
When He is seen — both the higher and the lower.

documents.sanskrit:
हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम् ।
तच्छुभ्रं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिस्तद्यदात्मविदो विदुः
documents.text:
In the highest golden sheath
Is Brahma, without stain, without parts.
Brilliant is It, the light of lights —
That which knowers of the Soul (Atman) do know !

documents.sanskrit:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं
नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं
तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति
documents.text:
The sun shines not there, nor the moon and stars;
These lightnings shine not, much less this [earthly] fire !
After Him, as He shines, doth everything shine.
This whole world is illumined with His light.

documents.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैवेदममृतं पुरस्ताद् ब्रह्म पश्चाद् ब्रह्म दक्षिणतश्चोत्तरेण ।
अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम्
documents.text:
Brahma, indeed, is this immortal. Brahma before,
Brahma behind, to right and to left.
Stretched forth below and above,
Brahma, indeed, is this whole world, this widest extent.

documents.sanskrit:
द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते ।
तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्ति अनश्नन्नन्योऽभिचाकशीति
documents.text:
Two birds, fast bound companions,
Clasp close the self-same tree.
Of these two, the one eats sweet fruit;
The other looks on without eating.

documents.sanskrit:
समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः ।
जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः
documents.text:
On the self-same tree a person, sunken,
Grieves for his impotence, deluded ;
When he sees the other, the Lord (is), contented,
And his greatness, he becomes freed from sorrow.

documents.sanskrit:
यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् ।
तदा विद्वान्पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति
documents.text:
When a seer sees the brilliant
Maker, Lord, Person, the Brahma-source,
Then, being a knower, shaking off good and evil,
Stainless, he attains supreme identity ( samya ) [with Him].

documents.sanskrit:
प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन्विद्वान्भवते नातिवादी ।
आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः
documents.text:
Truly, it is Life (Prana) that shines forth in all things!
Understanding this, one becomes a knower. There is no
superior speaker.
Having delight in the Soul (Atman), having pleasure in the
Soul, doing the rites,
Such a one is the best of Brahma-knowers.

documents.sanskrit:
सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् ।
अन्तः शरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः
documents.text:
This Soul (Atman) is obtainable by truth, by austerity ( tapas ),
By proper knowledge (jnana ), by the student’s life of chastity
( brahmacarya ) constantly [practised].
Within the body, consisting of light, pure is He
Whom the ascetics (yati), with imperfections done away,
behold.

documents.sanskrit:
सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः ।
येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम्
documents.text:
Truth alone conquers, not falsehood.
By truth is laid out the path leading to the gods ( devayana )
By which the sages whose desire is satisfied ascend
To where is the highest repository of truth.

documents.sanskrit:
बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्माच्च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति ।
दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यन्त्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम्
documents.text:
Vast, heavenly, of unthinkable form,
And more minute than the minute, It shines forth.
It is farther than the far, yet here near at hand,
Set down in the secret place [of the heart], even here among
those who behold [It].

documents.sanskrit:
न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा ।
ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः
documents.text:
Not by sight is It grasped, not even by speech,
Not by any other sense-organs ( deva ), austerity, or work.
By the peace of knowledge ( jnana-prasada ), one’s nature
purified —
In that way, however, by meditating, one does behold Him
who is without parts.

documents.sanskrit:
एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश ।
प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा
documents.text:
That subtile Soul (Atman) is to be known by thought ( cetas )
Wherein the senses [prana) fivefoldly have entered.
The whole of men’s thinking is interwoven with the senses.
When that is purified, the Soul (Atman) shines forth.

documents.sanskrit:
यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् ।
तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामांस्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेत्भूतिकामः
documents.text:
Whatever world a man of purified nature makes clear in mind,
And whatever desires he desires for himself —
That world he wins, those desires too.
Therefore he who is desirous of welfare should praise the
knower of the Soul (Atman).

documents.sanskrit:
स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् ।
उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः
documents.text:
He knows that Supreme Brahma-abode,
Founded on which the whole world shines radiantly.
They who, being without desire, worship the Person (Purusha)
And are wise, pass beyond the seed (sukra) [of rebirth] here.

documents.sanskrit:
कामान्यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र ।
पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः
documents.text:
He who in fancy forms desires,
Because of his desires is born [again] here and there.
But of him whose desire is satisfied, who is a perfected soul
( krtatman ),
All desires even here on earth vanish away.

documents.sanskrit:
नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन ।
यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम्

नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् ।
एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम
documents.text:
This Soul (Atman) is not to be obtained by one destitute of
fortitude,
Nor through heedlessness, nor through a false notion of
austerity ( tapas ).
But he who strives by these means, provided he knows —
Into his Brahma-abode this Soul (Atman) enters.

documents.sanskrit:
सम्प्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः
ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीराः युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति
documents.text:
Attaining Him, the seers (rsi) who are satisfied with knowledge,
Who are perfected souls ( krtatman ), from passion free (vita-raga), tranquil —
Attaining Him who is the universally omnipresent, those wise,
Devout souls ( yuktatman ) into the All itself do enter.

documents.sanskrit:
वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः ।
ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे
documents.text:
They who have ascertained the meaning of the Vedanta-knowledge,
Ascetics ( yati ) with natures purified .through the application of
renunciation ( samnyasa-yoga ) —
They in the Brahma-worlds at the end of time
Are all liberated beyond death.

documents.sanskrit:
गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु ।
कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा परेऽव्यये सर्व एकीभवन्ति
documents.text:
Gone are the fifteen parts according to their station,
Even all the sense-organs ( deva ) in their corresponding
divinities !
One’s deeds ( karman ) and the self that consists of understanding ( vijnana-maya atman ) —
All become unified in the supreme Imperishable.

documents.sanskrit:
यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय ।
तथा विद्वान्नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्
documents.text:
As the flowing rivers in the ocean
Disappear, quitting name and form,
So the knower, being liberated from name and form,
Goes unto the heavenly Person, higher than the high.

documents.sanskrit:
स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति ।
तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति
documents.text:
He, verily, who knows that supreme Brahma, becomes
